problem:
The function $y=f(x)$ satisfies the differential equation 

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=y+{e}^{x}.
$$

 

Given that the point $P(-1,0)$ lies on the graph of the function, evaluate $\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}$ at $P.$

feedback.problem:
Consider the solution curves of the differential equation ${y}^{′}-{x}^{3}={y}^{2}-2x.$ Which of the following points are stationary points of their respective solution curve?

- $(-1,-1)$
- $(0,0)$
- $(1,1)$
feedback.worked_solution:
Recall that a stationary point of $y(x)$ is a point $x=c$ in the domain of $y$ such that ${y}^{′}(c)=0.$ 

First, we make ${y}^{′}$ the subject of the equation.

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}-{x}^{3}={y}^{2}-2x\,⟹\,{y}^{′}={x}^{3}+{y}^{2}-2x\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we substitute the coordinates of our points into the differential equation and calculate the value of the derivative: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{{y}^{′}|}_{(-1,-1)} & ={({x}^{3}+{y}^{2}-2x)|}_{(-1,-1)} \\  & =(-1)^{3}+(-1)^{2}-2(-1) \\  & =2 \\  & \ne 0\,\times  \\ {{y}^{′}|}_{(0,0)} & ={({x}^{3}+{y}^{2}-2x)|}_{(0,0)} \\  & =(0)^{3}+(0)^{2}-2(0) \\  & =0\,✓ \\ {{y}^{′}|}_{(1,1)} & ={({x}^{3}+{y}^{2}-2x)|}_{(1,1)} \\  & =(1)^{3}+(1)^{2}-2(1) \\  & =0\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only."
